first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Both memory_86 and memory_31 demonstrated that reductions in onboarding friction (shortening flow and cutting required fields) produced durable lifts in activation and early adoption. These are directly applicable to the current decline. While promotional_pricing addresses the competitor threat, it risks a race-to-bottom that erodes long-term revenue quality and margins. Referral_incentive works in established cohorts but doesn't address the current activation funnel problem. enterprise_sales_assist is orthogonal to the core SMB activation challenge. Verifying memory_86 and memory_31 will confirm the magnitude and persistence of onboarding simplification effects, allowing a confident standard_experiment. Activation_messaging (memory_91) is a complementary lever that can amplify onboarding improvements. This approach preserves long-term unit economics while addressing the immediate activation decline, and avoids promotional pricing dependency that would be hard to unwind.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms both onboarding interventions drove measurable lifts: exp_86 showed +13% completion, -2.1 day time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention; exp_31 delivered +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB segment with only -1% retention dip. Current situation shows 4% onboarding completion decline and 6% activation decline QoQ. A standard_experiment applying simplified signup (exp_31 pattern) combined with activation messaging (memory_91) directly addresses both metrics. This is lower-risk than promotional pricing (which erodes margins and invites margin compression spirals) and more immediate than referral incentives (which benefit established cohorts, not acquisition funnel). The verified +3% to +4% qualified revenue uplift and activation gains justify immediate rollout. Preserves uncertainty by running as controlled experiment rather than full rollout, allowing measurement of segment performance and retention impact before scale.
